fixes.explanation: Moses it is, friend. The Levite heads say it plainly: "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). They aren't asking for a favor here. They're holding up a command that was already given, like walking into the bakery with the receipt in hand.

Cities to live in! The Levite heads say the LORD commanded "…that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). Pasturelands for their livestock come along with them. Forty-eight cities by the end (Joshua 21:41). FORTY-EIGHT. Somebody is going to need a very long list of housewarming parties, baker.

Tents near the tabernacle is a good guess, because the LORD did tell the Levites to camp around the tabernacle in the wilderness (Numbers 1:53). But that isn't what they ask for here. They say the LORD commanded that they be given "…cities in which to live, together with pasturelands for our livestock." (Joshua 21:2). So the answer is cities, friend, not tents.

That's right, baker. The text says the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and pasturelands "…out of their own inheritance…" (Joshua 21:3). Think about that. Nobody hands over part of their own land and then writes a complaint to the manager. They did it "…by the command of the LORD…" and they gave from what was already theirs. Then the lots begin, and the first one comes out for the Kohathite clans (Joshua 21:4).
